nodes.name: Carbon cloth pretreatment
nodes.procedure: The piece of carbon cloth (about 2×4 cm) was carefully cleaned with acetone, ultra-pure water and absolute ethanol in the ultrasonic bath for 15 min each time sequentially. At last, the carbon cloth was vacuum-dried overnight.

nodes.name: Co8FeV-LDH@CC hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 2.56 mmol (0.7450 g) Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O, 0.32 mmol (0.1293 g) Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O and 0.32 mmol (0.05024 g) VCl₃ were dispersed into 35 mL ultra-pure water by stirring for 15 min. Next, 0.3 g urea was added into the above transparent solution. Then, the mixed solution and the pretreated carbon cloth were transferred into a 50 mL polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) reaction kettle and heated at 120°C for 12 h. After cooling to room temperature, Co₈FeV@CC was obtained by vacuum drying; the precipitate was collected by centrifugation followed by freeze drying for 24 h.

nodes.name: α-Co(OH)2@CC electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The solution consists of 0.02 M Co(NO3)2·6H2O and 0.1 M NH4Cl was prepared. Then, the chronopotentiometry was used at the constant current density of 5 mA cm⁻² for 1 h to carry out the electrodeposition on carbon cloth (area ~4 cm²) using Pt counter electrode and Hg/HgO reference electrode. Finally, the product was dried overnight at 60°C.

nodes.name: γ-FeOOH@CC electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The electrolyte solution is composed of 0.1 M FeSO4 and 0.05 M NaNO3. The chronoamperometry was utilized at the constant potential of 0.8 V (vs. Hg/HgO) for 1 h to conduct the electrodeposition of γ-FeOOH on carbon cloth.

nodes.name: VOOH hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 2 mmol (0.2340 g) NH4VO3 was dissolved in 45 mL ultra-pure water with continuous stirring. Subsequently, 1 mL HCl (1 M) was added into the above solution at a rate of 1 drop per minute during which the solution turned into transparent yellow. Then, 5 mL hydrazine hydrate (85%) was added into the solution with constant stirring and the solution became turbid accompanied with its color changed to gray from yellow. The solution was thereafter moved into a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave and heated at 120°C for 8 h. The sample was washed with ultra-pure water and absolute ethanol for several times after it was cooled off to room temperature, which was followed by the overnight vacuum drying at 60°C.

nodes.procedure: 5.0 mg powders were dispersed in a solution consisting of 475 μL absolute ethanol, 475 μL deionized water and 50 μL Nafion (5 wt %) in the ultrasonic bath for 30 min. nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show Co8FeV@CC nanosheets uniformly and densely anchored on carbon fiber surface with irregular edges.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FESEM images in Fig. 1b and e display the micromorphology of Co8FeV@CC. Obviously, its nanosheets are uniformly and densely anchored on the surface of the carbon fiber...

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of Co8FeV@CC shows lattice fringes with interplanar spacings of 0.27 nm and 0.38 nm corresponding to (012) and (006) planes of LDH materials; nanosheet thickness is 1.4 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution transmission electron microscope (HRTEM) image displayed in Fig. 1c indicates... lattice fringes... measured to be 0.27 nm and 0.38 nm... (012) and (006) crystal plane... thickness of the monodispersed nanosheet was measured to be approximately 1.4 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping confirms uniform distribution of Co, Fe, V on Co8FeV@CC carbon fiber surface; relative mass fractions are Co 81.869 wt%, Fe 8.910 wt%, V 9.221 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS mapping (Fig. 1f) shows that Co, Fe, and V are uniformly distributed on the surface of the carbon fiber... relative mass fractions of Co, Fe, and V in Co8FeV@CC were calculated at 81.869%, 8.910%, and 9.221%, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co8FeV@CC exhibits LDH crystal structure consistent with JCPDS No. 50-0235; diffraction peaks positively shift ~0.5° compared to α-Co(OH)₂ due to interlayer anions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co8FeV@CC exhibits a similar crystal structure with Co4V@CC and Co4Fe@CC (Fig. 2a), which complies with JCPDS No. 50-0235... diffraction peaks of LDHs positively shift ~0.5° compared with those of α-Co(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-IR confirms layered LDH structure with NO₃⁻ intercalation (intense band at 1500 cm⁻¹) and hydrogen-bonded hydroxyl groups (broad band ~3450 cm⁻¹) in Co8FeV@CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Fig. 2c, the intense bands at 1500 cm⁻¹ are attributed to NO₃⁻... broad bands around 3450 cm⁻¹ are ascribed to the stretching of the hydrogen-bonded hydroxyl groups...
